files.content:
# Portfolio Standard gate — generated by @caistech/portfolio-migrator
#
# Runs typecheck + lint + build, then route + auth smoke tests against the
# preview deploy URL. Fails the action (and blocks Vercel promotion) on any
# non-zero exit.
#
# Closes Portfolio Standard:
#   R1  — Auth four-leg pattern (auth smoke step)
#   R10 — No verbatim Postgres errors (errorResponse helper, enforced at code level)
#   R13 — Route smoke test on every deploy (route smoke step)

name: portfolio-gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master]
  push:
    branches: [main, master]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    env:
      PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL: ${{ vars.PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: lts/*
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then
            corepack enable
            pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          elif [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
            npm ci
          else
            npm install
          fi
        env:
          GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN }}

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck --if-present

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint --if-present

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build --if-present

      - name: Verify preview URL is set
        run: |
          if [ -z "$PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL" ]; then
            echo "::error::PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL is not set. Wire it via repo vars or a preview-deploy step."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Preview URL: $PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL"

      - name: Route smoke test (Portfolio Standard R13)
        run: |
          npx --no-install portfolio-gate-smoke-routes \
            --config routes.config.json \
            --base-url "$PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL"

      - name: Auth smoke test (Portfolio Standard R1/R4)
        run: |
          npx --no-install portfolio-gate-smoke-auth \
            --config auth.config.json \
            --base-url "$PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL"

steps.title: Scrub vendor identity references
steps.description: Replace literal references to operator handle / mobile / Calendly / email with process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_VENDOR_* references. Marked NOTE because the exact substitution depends on the call site — string template vs JSX text vs prop value all need slightly different syntax. Review each before applying.
steps.body:
1 occurrence of vendor identity strings were detected. Replace each with a process.env reference and add the placeholder to .env.example.

| File | Find | Replace with |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/seed-abc-manufacturer.ts` | `mcmdennis` | `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_VENDOR_HANDLE ?? ''}` |

These are NOT auto-applied because the exact substitution depends on the call site:
- Inside a string template: `\${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_VENDOR_EMAIL ?? ''}`
- Inside JSX text: `{process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_VENDOR_EMAIL}`
- Inside a prop value: `vendorEmail={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_VENDOR_EMAIL}`

Apply by hand, verify with `npx portfolio-gate-audit-vendor-leak`, then commit.

# LingoPure — environment variables (.env.example, safe to commit)
# Copy this to .env.local and fill in real values. .env.local is gitignored.

# ── Supabase ──
# Project: nbvprbaumwmfczsfcyrv (https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/nbvprbaumwmfczsfcyrv)
# NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix is required so the URL is inlined into the browser bundle.
# Server-only code (middleware, server.ts) falls back to SUPABASE_URL if the
# prefixed variant is missing — keep both for backwards compat with older code.
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://nbvprbaumwmfczsfcyrv.supabase.co
SUPABASE_URL=https://nbvprbaumwmfczsfcyrv.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=
# Service role key — server-only, used by webhook routes / migrations / RLS-bypass jobs.
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=

# ── LLM ──
# Anthropic Claude (model: claude-sonnet-4-6) — gap scoring rubric, lesson generation
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
# OpenAI Whisper — post-session recording transcription (Phase 2)
OPENAI_API_KEY=

# ── Voice agent (ElevenLabs ConvAI, replaces Vapi from briefing) ──
# Set after you create the discovery agent via @caistech/elevenlabs-convai
ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=
ELEVENLABS_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID=

# ── ClassIn SDK (commercial credentials from EEO) ──
# Until obtained, /classroom/[sessionId] renders the placeholder iframe.
CLASSIN_APP_ID=
CLASSIN_APP_SECRET=

# ── Email / nudges ──
# Resend — transactional email (signup confirmation, password reset, nudges).
# Used by Supabase Auth SMTP (configured automatically via supabase/config.toml + `supabase config push`)
# and by @caistech/nudge-core in Phase 2.
RESEND_API_KEY=
# Verified Resend domain — sender becomes noreply@$SMTP_FROM_DOMAIN.

# ── Supabase Management API ──
# Personal access token from https://supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens
# Required to run `supabase config push` and any setup script that hits the Management API.
SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=

# ── Optional / future ──
# GitHub Packages token for installing private @caistech/* packages
# (set in shell, not committed). Required for: npm install @caistech/elevenlabs-convai
# GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN=

# Portfolio Standard R11 — vendor identity routed through env vars.

NEXT_PUBLIC_VENDOR_CALENDLY=""
NEXT_PUBLIC_VENDOR_INSTAGRAM=""

steps.title: Swap raw auth pages to <AuthForm/>
steps.description: Raw <input type="password"> was found in the repo. The Portfolio Standard requires <AuthForm/> for R1 compliance. Marked NOTE because the swap surface depends on per-product branding / redirect URLs / analytics hooks.
steps.body:
Replace every raw login / signup / forgot-password / reset-password page
with `<AuthForm/>` from `@caistech/corporate-components` (shipped in 0.2.0).

`<AuthForm/>` bakes in all four R1 legs (forgot-password link, password
visibility toggle, magic-link, email verification) plus mobile-first
responsive defaults (R2), 44 px tap targets, and a built-in
explanatory header per mode (R3).

### Example: `app/login/page.tsx`

```tsx
'use client';
import { AuthForm } from '@caistech/corporate-components';
import { createBrowserClient } from '@supabase/ssr';

export default function LoginPage() {
  const supabase = createBrowserClient(
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!
  );
  return (
    <AuthForm
      mode="login"
      supabase={supabase}
      brandName="lingopure"
      redirectTo="/dashboard"
    />
  );
}
```

### What to review before swapping

- **Redirect URL.** Confirm `redirectTo` matches your post-login surface.
- **Custom branding.** If the existing login page has a hero / logo / illustration,
  pass it via the `<AuthForm/>`'s `brandName` + slot props rather than wrapping
  raw HTML around the form.
- **Analytics.** If the existing form fires a custom event on submit, wire it via
  the `onSuccess` callback rather than re-implementing the form.
- **Server actions.** `<AuthForm/>` uses the Supabase browser client directly.
  If your existing flow goes through a server action, you can keep that handler
  and pass a thin `onSubmit` to the form — but the default direct-client path is
  what the auth smoke test exercises.

This swap is **note-only** — the migrator does not auto-generate the new
pages because of the customisation surface above. Apply the swap by hand
and verify with `npx portfolio-gate-smoke-auth` before landing.

### Files containing raw password inputs

- `src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`
- `src/app/(auth)/signup/page.tsx`

steps.title: Replace USING (true) RLS policies
steps.description: Migrations contain USING (true) on data-bearing tables. NOTE-only — the replacement owner column depends on the table's tenancy model.
steps.body:
One or more migrations contain `USING (true)` against a data-bearing
table — this violates Portfolio Standard R9.

`USING (true)` allows every authenticated row to read every other row's
data, which is a Privacy Act exposure on REGULATED and REVENUE tier
products. The naive-tester sweep on 2026-05-19 found this exact pattern
on Connexions, Universal Interviews, Platform-Trust, and Longtail-AIVS.

### How to fix

For each violation, write a new migration that:

1. `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS <name> ON <table>;`
2. `CREATE POLICY <name> ON <table> FOR <ops> TO <role>
   USING (auth.uid() = <owner_column>);`

The owner column varies per table — `owner_id`, `user_id`, `org_id`,
`tenant_id` are all common. The migrator cannot infer the correct column
safely, so this step is **note-only**.

### Verify

After applying, run:

```bash
npx portfolio-gate-audit-rls
```

It must report `PASS` before the deploy promotes.

### Locations

- `supabase/migrations/0001_initial_schema.sql:37`
- `supabase/migrations/0010_roles_baselines.sql:51`
- `supabase/migrations/0010_roles_baselines.sql:76`
- `supabase/migrations/0014_teachers_departments.sql:39`
- `supabase/migrations/0014_teachers_departments.sql:73`
- `supabase/migrations/0014_teachers_departments.sql:97`
